title: Black Mac's protection and what a Creole is
summary: Dallas toughs took to Albert as Black Mac's buddy; he defines Creole as a mixture of races.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: It was only about six blocks from the place where I was playing, which was predominantly the Negro neighborhood. And they had this railroad track down there, as you recall, it was called Central Track. And that's where all the thugs lived. And I guess I was too younger to realize the danger. So he told me, you better get on home and get on home and run quickly, right quickly, because some of you niggas will take your head off. He thought I was a white boy. Yeah. So I said, okay, I thanked him so much, so I left and I went. But my situation was this. It looked like all of the bad characters in the time would take up with me. I mean, real bad, shady characters that everybody was afraid of. Yeah. And I imagine it helped me a lot because one time I was up in what they call North Dallas. And this fellow was always six, about six feet, five inches tall. They called him Black Mac. And boy, he was tough. I mean, tough. And so the fellow said, oh, oh, he said, oh, mess with that little fellow there. I said, that's that Creole from New Orleans. And that's Black Mac's close buddies. He said, if you mess with him, Black Mac will get you. Oh, young and, you know, like this, you just laugh at things like that. Yeah. Later on in years, you realize, well, hell, man, this was something on your side. And it looked like it was my fortune or my good fortune, even in New York, to meet up with these guys. They said, take a liking to me, you see. And, well, that's it. A good friendly association treated me like a king. Wouldn't let nobody call me or nothing else. What is a Creole, anyway? Well, no, that's a debatable subject. My wife loves to call herself a Creole. They call me a Creole. The way that I see it, it is a mixture of races. The Creole has everything. We have Indians, we have Filipinas, we have Turks. We have Italians, which you know my name. I told you, Dominic, you would have pirate on the ship. Come from the Dominican Republic, Gene Defeat. That's where this creation of color has come in to call you a Creole. Now, there have been some real dark, dark Creoles. They call them Creoles because they're from the original Creole family. And sometimes a family, it goes, you see a family that has three or four real light-complected ones. And you look again, you see a dark one, but he's still the full brother and sister. Well, I think that's a debatable item, and I don't like to dwell too much on it. Because I might say something that might offend somebody, which I would most certainly not want to do. But that's the only answer that I can give for him.
